keyVerseText: For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.
rootMeaning: The word ἀμήν (amḗn) originates from the Hebrew אָמֵן (ʼâmên), which conveys the ideas of firmness, faithfulness, and truth. Its root meaning emphasizes being sure or reliable, extending beyond a mere affirmation to encompass trustworthiness and steadfastness. This foundational sense enriches the common English glosses like 'amen' or 'verily' by highlighting a profound assurance and confidence in what is affirmed.
usageInScripture: Across Scripture, ἀμήν appears 152 times, predominantly translated as 'Verily' (89 occurrences) and 'Amen' (50 occurrences), with occasional renderings like 'verily' or 'the Amen.' This consistent use as a solemn affirmation or declaration underscores its role as a marker of truth and certainty. Whether initiating statements or concluding prayers, its presence signals a firm endorsement of the truthfulness of the words spoken.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἀμήν in its original sense enriches our appreciation of biblical truth as not only verbally affirmed but inherently trustworthy and steadfast. In the Christian faith, this assurance reflects God's unchanging nature and the reliability of His promises. The word's Hebrew roots in faithfulness remind believers that God's word is firm and dependable, inviting a response of confident trust. Thus, ἀμήν is more than a liturgical conclusion; it is a declaration of divine faithfulness and the certainty of God's covenantal truth.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 5:18, Jesus declares, 'For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.' The use of ἀμήν here underscores the absolute certainty and unchanging nature of God's law. By prefacing His statement with this word, Jesus affirms that His teaching rests on a foundation of unshakable truth, assuring believers that God's promises and commands will be perfectly accomplished.
